name: Button
description: A clickable control that starts an action: saving a form, confirming a choice, opening a dialog. Its emphasis levels signal how important an action is, so the choice of variant is the main decision when you use it.
whenToUse: The user needs to make something happen on the current page, like saving, confirming, or opening a dialog.
A view needs one obvious primary action.
whenNotToUse: The control takes the user to another page or URL. Use a Link; the link variant only looks like a link and still triggers an action.

variant.default: The one main action in a view.
variant.secondary: A supporting action that sits beside the main one.
variant.destructive: An action that deletes something or cannot be undone.
variant.outline: A quieter action that still needs a visible edge.
variant.ghost: The quietest action, for toolbars and dense layouts.
variant.link: An action that reads as inline text.

size.md: The default size for most uses.
size.lg: For hero moments that need extra presence.

states.default: At rest and ready to be clicked.
states.hover: The pointer is over the button and it lightens to invite a click.
states.focus: The button has keyboard focus and shows a focus ring.
states.active: The button is being pressed, and its fill brightens until it's released.
states.disabled: Can't be clicked or tabbed to.
states.loading: The action is running; a spinner replaces the leading icon until it finishes.

dos: Lead the label with a verb.
Keep one primary button per view.
Keep labels to about three words.
donts: Don't use a button to navigate. Use a Link.
Don't stack two primary buttons in one view.
Don't disable a button without telling the user why.

notes: An icon-only button needs an aria-label so screen readers can announce it.
A disabled or loading button can't take keyboard focus. Say why it is unavailable somewhere a screen reader will reach.
